newsitem.title: INDIA: Transcript of last talk with doomed airliners.
newsitem.headline: Transcript of last talk with doomed airliners.

text.p: Following is the transcript of the final conversation between Air Traffic Control at New Delhi airport and the two pilots involved in the world's worst mid-air collision which killed some 350 people.

An Indian Civil Aviation Ministry official read out the transcript to a news conference on Wednesday, almost 24 hours after the collision between a Saudi Arabian Airlines Boeing 747 and a Kazakh Ilyushin IL-76 freighter.

Note - Most of the numbers refer to altitude. "Level 140" means a height of 14,000 feet, the altitude the Saudi Airliner was told to climb to as it took off for Dhahran and Jeddah. The KazAir freighter was preparing to land.
SA 763: Approaching level 140 for higher. Await.
Radar: Maintain level 140. Stand by for higher.
Radar: KZA 1907, report distance from DPN.
Radar: Roger. Maintain 150. Identified traffic 12 o'clock reciprocal Saudi Boeing 747 14 miles. Report when in sight.
KZA 1907: Kazakh 1907 -- Repeat, how many miles?
Radar: Traffic is 13 miles at level 140.
